name: Garlic Butter Shrimp over Rice
pitch: Simple, fast, and deeply satisfying — buttery garlicky shrimp over fluffy rice is a weeknight hero that comes together in under 20 minutes.
steps: Cook your rice according to package directions.
While rice cooks, melt 2 tablespoons of butter in a skillet over medium-high heat and add 4–5 minced garlic cloves.
Add the shrimp in a single layer, season with salt and pepper, and cook 1–2 minutes per side until pink and curled.
Squeeze a little vinegar (or a splash of water with a pinch of salt) to deglaze the pan if you'd like a bit of a sauce.
Spoon the shrimp and all that garlicky butter over your rice and serve.
toolSuggestion: A wide skillet or sauté pan

name: Soy-Glazed Shrimp Fried Rice
pitch: A takeout-style fried rice that uses what you have and tastes like you planned it all along — soy sauce and a hot pan do most of the work.
steps: Cook rice and let it cool for a few minutes — or use leftover rice if you have it, as it fries up best.
Heat oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat until very hot.
Add shrimp, season with salt and pepper, cook 1–2 minutes per side, then set aside.
Add a little more oil to the same pan, toss in the rice, and stir-fry for 3–4 minutes, pressing it against the pan to get some crispy bits.
Add 2–3 tablespoons of soy sauce, stir well, return the shrimp to the pan, toss everything together, and serve hot.
Note: eggs and green onions would make this even better if you happen to have them.
toolSuggestion: A wok or the largest skillet you own

name: Spiced Shrimp Rice Bowl with Vinegar Drizzle
pitch: This is a bright, slightly tangy rice bowl with warm spiced shrimp — simple but it has a little personality that makes it feel special.
steps: Cook your rice and season it lightly with a tiny splash of vinegar and a pinch of salt once done — this gives it a subtle brightness.
Toss shrimp with a little oil, garlic powder, cumin or paprika (whatever dried spices you have), salt, and pepper.
Cook shrimp in a hot oiled skillet 1–2 minutes per side until cooked through.
Spoon rice into a bowl, top with shrimp, and drizzle with a little more vinegar mixed with oil as a quick dressing.
Note: sliced avocado, a fried egg, or any fresh vegetables on hand would round this out nicely.
toolSuggestion: A small mixing bowl for tossing the shrimp in spices
